parts.note: a portion is a piece, a share of something

explanation.surface: Every person present is told to help themselves to one serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will take' only links definition and wordplay. A PIECE, one portion apiece, means each.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of things shared out, it means per person, one to every individual.

parts.note: the letter A, like the word an

explanation.walkthrough: Both 'An' and 'A' are indefinite articles: the clue asks what kind of word they are.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the indefinite determiner a or an belongs to this part of speech.

indicators.note: about means turned around and moved, so the letters of still rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone keeps grading cruelty to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the anagram of STILLRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistreat someone is to abuse them, treating them cruelly.

explanation.surface: Trusting in a bank loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in making' links the two senses: to credit a story is to believe it, and credit is money lent.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a claim is to accept it as true, and credit is money advanced on trust.

clue.text: A shrub or building gives shelter

indicators.note: building here means constructing something new, so the letters of a shrub or are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A bush or a shed offers somewhere to keep out of the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' signals the anagram of ASHRUBOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour a fugitive is to give them refuge, a verb of protection.

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A choice between a fish and something made from seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' only links. The gar or garfish has a long beak-like snout.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly extracted from red algae, used to set foods and grow bacteria.

clue.text: Jokey talk that's attractive only in the young

parts.words: that's attractive only in the young
parts.note: something attractive only in youth is ..., the phrase split into three words

explanation.surface: Playful banter is charming in youngsters only.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BAD IN AGE: what is attractive only in the young is bad in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Banter is light teasing conversation.

clue.text: Not Alexander's way to deal with a knotty problem!

definitions.text: Not Alexander's way to deal with a knotty problem!

parts.words: Not Alexander's way to deal with a knotty problem!
parts.note: Alexander the Great cut the Gordian knot with his sword rather than loosening it by hand

explanation.surface: Alexander the Great faced a tangled puzzle and handled it his own way.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says Alexander, unable to undo the Gordian knot, sliced through it: the patient way he spurned was to loosen it.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosening a knot by hand is the patient solution Alexander rejected for his sword.

clue.text: Taking issue about covering the cheese

annotationWithheld.why: Taking issue about covering the cheese (7) for STILTON: SON (issue) around TILT needs TILT from 'Taking' or 'about', neither of which gives it; 'Taking issue' as TILT would use 'issue' twice
annotationWithheld.clue: Taking issue about covering the cheese

clue.text: Showed some inclination for armed combat?

explanation.surface: Someone leaning slightly, or someone itching for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: To tilt is to lean, and also to joust: knights tilted at each other with lances.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning over is showing a slope, and tilting was the jousting of mounted knights with lances.

clue.text: Lawless characters set it back it would appear

parts.note: a set of people, a group, is a band
taken as written

indicators.note: back means the second it is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: Outlaws seem to have pushed some scheme backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the second IT into TI; 'would appear' just links. BANDITTI is an old plural of bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandits are outlaws and robbers, lawless people by trade.

indicators.note: troublesome suggests the letters of tears up are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tearing up a lawn that is causing problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears up' looks like the action, but it is the fodder; 'troublesome' signals its anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Land covered with grass for grazing animals.

explanation.surface: A woolly garment named after a place.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardigan is a town in west Wales; the button-up jacket is named after the Earl of Cardigan.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttoned knitted jacket, and a small coastal town in Wales.

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so a possible arrangement of the letters of nicest is wanted

explanation.surface: A small animal blessed with the sweetest temperament imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' reads as temperament, but it means arrangement: 'possible disposition' signals the anagram of NICEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug or beetle is a tiny six-legged animal.

clue.text: Colour is a factor in some degree

indicators.note: in means the factor is placed inside the degree

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is one degree a graduate might hold
a factor is an agent who acts for another

explanation.surface: Hue is something that plays a part to an extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'factor' reads as a contributing element but means an agent, one who does business for another.
explanation.definitionFit: A purplish-red dye and shade.

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to be made to do something is to be forced

explanation.surface: An army driven back somewhere in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retreat' turns MADE round. The definition describes a place: Edam is a town in North Holland.
explanation.definitionFit: A town found in the Netherlands, famous for its cheese.

clue.text: Adjust rate and things should be different

indicators.note: the letters of rate and things are to be made different, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to change a price so that circumstances alter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate' reads as a price to be adjusted, but it is only fodder; 'should be different' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something right or level is to correct its position.

clue.text: Time to get up put off

parts.note: tempo is time or pace in music
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Time to get out of bed, but postponed again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to stall and delay a decision to gain time.

parts.note: SM is a sergeant major, a senior non-commissioned officer
irking means annoying, wearing someone down

explanation.surface: A sergeant major is tiresome but keeps grinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinning in a smug or self-satisfied way.

clue.text: Examination for which someone's always inexplicably late

definitions.text: Examination for which someone's always inexplicably late

parts.words: Examination for which someone's always inexplicably late
parts.note: the person examined is the late one, late meaning dead, and the inquiry is into why they died

explanation.surface: A test that some candidate habitually turns up late for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' reads as tardy but means deceased: this examination is held on a body to find out how death happened.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopsy examines a corpse after death to establish its cause.

clue.text: Mislead retiring minister in audacious fashion

indicators.note: in means the turned minister goes inside the audacious word

parts.note: pert means cheeky, bold and audacious

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the word for the minister is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend, a minister of the church

explanation.surface: A clergyman stepping down boldly misleads people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like a minister leaving office, but it is the reversal signal; 'fashion' belongs with 'audacious' as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervert justice is to divert it from its proper course, leading it astray.

clue.text: The medico goes in like a man

indicators.note: goes in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: The doctor arrives looking like an ordinary fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (medical officer) is the crossword's usual doctor. Amos is a man's name, borne by an Old Testament prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: A male given name, borne by a Hebrew prophet.

explanation.surface: Repairs to a kitchen basin.
explanation.walkthrough: To settle is to fix or decide, and also to sink down, as sediment settles.
explanation.definitionFit: Settles means decides or arranges for good, and also subsides or goes down gradually.

clue.text: : Showing bad spirit over work can cause strike

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
an act is a deed, a piece of work

explanation.surface: A bad attitude at work may lead to an industrial walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action but means a collision or blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The force of one object hitting another, a collision.

explanation.surface: A journalist covering a loud disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: A report is an account written about something, and also the bang of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To file an account of events, and the sharp bang of a shot or explosion.

indicators.note: organising means arranging, so the letters of a plot are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek thinker plans a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' signals the anagram of APLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian philosopher who wrote the Republic.

indicators.note: ordered means put in a different order, so the letters of a stout MP are rearranged

explanation.surface: A portly politician gave instructions for a squashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like 'commanded' but signals the anagram of ASTOUTMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp out a rebellion is to suppress it by force.

explanation.surface: Units of length, or what someone stands on.
explanation.walkthrough: Feet are units of length, and also what a person stands on.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial units of twelve inches, and the parts at the end of the legs a person stands upon.

clue.text: The Inspector is no longer a worker underground

parts.note: ex means former, something that no longer is
a miner works down a pit

explanation.surface: The inspector once had a job down a coal mine.
explanation.walkthrough: EX is the prefix for 'former', standing for 'is no longer'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector checks and tests things, as an official assessor or invigilator does.

clue.text: Get 'the painter to phone. from the centre

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
to dial is to make a call on a telephone

explanation.surface: Instructions to have the artist ring head office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' suggests head office; it is the hub of a wheel. RA (Royal Academician) is the crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spokes spread outwards from a hub, and anything so arranged extends outward from a middle point.

parts.note: the missing last word of Ophelia's line about flowers in Hamlet, where pansies stand for remembrance of the mind

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank from Ophelia's flower speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Ophelia's full line is 'And there is pansies, that's for thoughts'; the name pansy comes from French pensée.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia's speech assigns pansies to musings of the mind, from French pensée.

indicators.note: some of means only part of the word songstresses is taken

explanation.surface: A few female singers are overwhelmed by expectations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run from inside songstresses. To stress, informally, is to worry and feel strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To get anxious and strained under demands, as in stressing over exams.
